title: Plant-based meat alternatives with the most protein

seo.title: Highest-protein plant-based meat alternatives
seo.meta_description: Compare TVP, seitan, tempeh, tofu, plant burgers and jackfruit by realistic protein amounts.
seo.search_intent: Find plant-based meat alternatives with the most protein

excerpt: The most protein-dense plant options tend to be dry TVP, seitan, tempeh and some formulated burgers. Firm tofu is still substantial, while young jackfruit is mainly a texture substitute.
content_html:
“Meat alternative” can describe texture, flavor, shape or nutrition—and those are not the same thing. Seitan and soy foods can be protein-dense; jackfruit can look meat-like while providing very little protein.

Dry TVP

A current plain TVP provides 12 g protein per 23 g dry. It exceeds 50 g/100 g dry, but that number drops per 100 g after hydration.

Seitan

The packaged seitan used here lists 18 g protein per 57 g, roughly 32 g/100 g. It is concentrated, though it contains gluten and can be salty.

Tempeh

USDA tempeh provides about 20.3 g/100 g.

Firm tofu

The calcium-set firm tofu reference provides 17.3 g/100 g. More watery tofu can be lower.

Formulated plant burgers

A current 113 g Beyond Burger lists 20 g protein. Vegetable-and-grain patties may provide much less.

Jackfruit is different

Young jackfruit is only around 2–2.6 g protein/100 g in technical references.

Protein is only one column

Also compare sodium, saturated fat, fiber, iron, calcium and B12.

faq.question: Which has the most protein?
faq.answer: Dry TVP is extremely concentrated, while seitan is among the highest ready-to-cook options.

faq.question: Does tempeh have more than tofu?
faq.answer: In these references, yes: 20.3 vs. 17.3 g/100 g.

faq.question: Are all veggie burgers high in protein?
faq.answer: No. Some provide around 20 g per patty; others much less.
